source_snapshot.procedure: Boot the OS; remove the heatsink or use a Peltier device to slowly heat the selected CPU through TWarning and TCritical; continue heating until the system resets; source clears logs first.
source_snapshot.criteria: System shuts down once TCritical is reached; BMC records CPUx over-temperature; applicable diagnostic-panel temperature LED, Aria LCD, CPU lightpath and front-panel fault light indicate the fault; later reboot and verify UEFI SEL records the over-temperature and reset.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL supplies the duplicate row's 25 warm reboots, which cannot exercise thermal warning/critical protection and exposes credentials.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED correctly rejects heatsink removal/unbounded heating and requires a calibrated interlocked fixture, but the exact terminal-action contradiction remains dependent on the target platform thermal contract.

old_problem: Procedure demands continued heat until reset, while Criteria demand shutdown at TCritical followed by a later reboot. These are distinct terminal states and stop conditions. The target CPU, thresholds, hysteresis, sensor lag, physical indicators, validated fixture, hard cutoff and post-trip recovery are also absent, and duplicate row 1527's warm-reboot procedure is unrelated.
disposition_reason: Official CPU documentation distinguishes adaptive thermal control/PROCHOT, critical-temperature notification intended to permit graceful shutdown, and catastrophic THERMTRIP hardware shutdown; it does not identify this platform's BMC TWarning/TCritical mapping or authorize reset in place of shutdown. Therefore the review cannot choose between the source's reset, shutdown and later operator reboot, nor define a safe terminal stop before damage. A parameterized evidence plan is prepared, but Pending and BLOCKED remain until the Project firmware/thermal owners provide a versioned state-transition contract and vendor-approved interlocked stimulus. Energized heatsink removal and open-loop `continue heating` remain prohibited; 25 warm reboots are excluded.
decision_basis: XLSX row 805, physical adjacent row 806, duplicate-code row 1527, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. Formal queue sequence 21 is row 807 / variant 96dfe392e26535d0.

Duplicate row 1527 / variant 3d6b813c4da3db07 is Sanity FW Matrix `Warm Reboot 25 times`, with a reboot-cycle script and 180-minute duration. It cannot create TWarning/TCritical, prove CPU protection or satisfy any physical indicator and remains independent.

Intel's architecture manual exposes thermal status, PROCHOT-related state, critical-temperature status/log bits and temperature readout. Critical-temperature status means immediate shutdown should occur and reliable operation is not guaranteed; it does not define this Project's BMC threshold names or chassis action.

Intel processor datasheets describe critical-temperature detection as intended for graceful shutdown before THERMTRIP, while catastrophic cooling failure asserts THERMTRIP and automatically shuts the package/system down. Thus generic authority contradicts treating all high-temperature terminal actions as an interchangeable reset.

BMC polling can lag a local junction ramp and the protection path under test cannot be the only safety mechanism. A qualified setup needs independent calibrated sensing and a hard cutoff below the platform damage boundary, plus bounded rate/dwell and restart inhibition.

The source's conditional LEDs/LCD/lightpath require an exact fitted-options matrix and real visual evidence. Absence may be N/A only with authoritative platform configuration, and API/SEL evidence cannot replace visual inspection.

ED-02 preserves duplicate identity; ED-15 requires SPEC-backed N/A; ED-17/ED-25 keep physical thermal fixtures and observations operator-controlled; ED-18/ED-30 prohibit invented limits; ED-19 protects SEL; ED-20/ED-23 require actual visual/state correlation; ED-28's isolation/tool/recovery principle applies to hazardous stimuli; ED-29 distinguishes terminal power states and OS Ready; ED-33 through ED-38 require safe authority and forbid false resolution.

test_case.test_command: BLOCKED — DO NOT EXECUTE. After the missing signed Project contract is supplied, export/hash logs without clearing, bind the exact CPU/sensor/threshold/indicator identities, validate fixture calibration and independent hard cutoff, and obtain point-of-action approval. A qualified thermal engineer may then apply one bounded ramp under synchronized independent-probe, BMC, fan, rail and host/power monitoring: capture TWarning and its mapped SEL/indicators; continue only if the Project matrix, sensor agreement and hard margin permit; capture TCritical and the exact authoritative terminal transition; hard-stop heat immediately at the defined action/abort, never continue toward an unspecified reset. A human records each fitted LED/LCD/lightpath. Keep restart inhibited until independent and BMC temperatures are below the approved recovery value and cooling/hardware inspection passes. Only then may the owner authorize the separately defined reboot/bring-up and UEFI SEL/OS Ready checks. No heatsink removal on an energized CPU, synthetic event as physical proof, 25 warm reboots, log clear, automatic restart or retry.
test_case.expected_result: Cannot be finalized until the Project selects the authoritative transition. The eventual contract must separately state TWarning reading/event/indicators, TCritical reading/event, exact shutdown/reset/hard-off and timing, physical indicator applicability, UEFI/BMC SEL content, cooldown/restart permission and final recovery. The observed result must exactly match that signed matrix, remain inside all independent safety bounds and restore the cooling assembly, sensors, power, BMC and OS health without damage.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No PASS is possible while reset versus shutdown, thresholds, safe fixture/cutoff or recovery remain unsigned. After resolution, PASS requires one authorized real physical thermal ramp with exact CPU/sensor identity, calibrated independent temperature, TWarning then TCritical within tolerance, matching raw BMC/UEFI events, all fitted visual indicators, exact terminal power transition, immediate stimulus stop, safe cooldown, hardware/cooling inspection, authorized reboot if applicable and full OS/BMC recovery. Warm reboots, event injection alone, BMC WebUI-only temperature, missing visual evidence, guessed thresholds, unexpected reset/shutdown, heat beyond the stop condition, log loss, N/A without SPEC, retry or incomplete recovery cannot pass.
safety_gate: Current gate is CLOSED. No thermal, cooling, threshold, reboot, power or log-clear action is authorized until the terminal-action and hard-interlock requirements are signed by the Project owners.
Never loosen/remove a heatsink on an energized CPU and never use open-loop heat-until-reset. Preserve that source text only as history, not an executable instruction.

The fixture needs an independently calibrated probe and hard cutoff that does not depend on BMC update rate, host software or the protection path under test; validate the interlock before the DUT is heated.

Abort below the vendor damage boundary on sensor disagreement, excessive ramp/dwell, cooling/fan/rail anomaly, missed event, unexpected state, lost OOB/independent telemetry or any physical distress. Remove stimulus and apply approved emergency cooling without awaiting software.
Preserve/hash complete logs before any mutation and preserve the first trip. Do not repeat, automatically reboot or continue to another CPU after any unexpected or ambiguous result.
Restart remains inhibited until temperatures, cooling installation/TIM/torque if disturbed, rails and visual inspection satisfy the recovery matrix and a human explicitly releases it.

test_case.recovery: Present recovery is intentionally non-executable because the safe terminal state is unresolved. The approved contract must require immediate independent stimulus removal and emergency cooling on anomaly, restart inhibition, preservation of BMC/UEFI/OOB evidence, and thermal/power-owner control. If the system unexpectedly resets or shuts down, do not reapply heat or auto-reboot; cool below the signed threshold, isolate power if the hard-interlock plan requires it, inspect the CPU socket/cooling/board/rails and reconcile the state. Any disturbed cooling assembly needs vendor TIM/torque restoration. Reboot only after explicit human release; then verify sensors, SEL, firmware, data/filesystem, BMC and OS Ready.

source_conflict.reason: Procedure reset, Criterion-1 shutdown and Criterion-7 later reboot are distinct authoritative states. Generic CPU standards distinguish protection layers but cannot select this platform's expected BMC TCritical transition; the conflict remains until a signed Project contract reconciles it.

external_authorities.title: Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual, Combined Volumes
external_authorities.application: Defines digital thermal status/PROCHOT and critical-temperature status/log behavior; critical status calls for immediate shutdown and warns reliable operation is not guaranteed. It does not define this Project's BMC thresholds or chassis terminal action.

external_authorities.title: 12th Generation Intel Core Processors Datasheet, Volume 1
external_authorities.application: Separates adaptive thermal control, critical-temperature graceful-shutdown intent and catastrophic THRMTRIP automatic shutdown. Used as evidence that reset, shutdown and silicon trip cannot be treated as one generic behavior; exact DUT family documentation remains required.

project_authority: Only the exact-platform thermal, CPU, firmware and power owners can resolve the terminal-action conflict and approve stimulus/recovery. Their decision must cite the target CPU/platform specification and cannot authorize energized heatsink removal, remove independent cutoff, turn a warm reboot into thermal coverage, waive missing visual evidence or confer PASS without the real bounded physical path.
